content.title: Timothée Chalamet Becomes Youngest Star with 3 Best Actor Oscar Nominations Since Marlon Brando
content.text: Timothée Chalamet is nominated for Best Actor at the 2026 Oscars for his role in Marty Supreme, and he is also nominated for Best Picture as a producer on the movie By Tommy McArdle Tommy McArdle is a writer-reporter on the Movies team at PEOPLE. Tommy joined PEOPLE in 2022. Published on January 22, 2026 10:06AM EST Timothée Chalamet on Jan. 11, 2026; Marlon Brando on April 1, 1955. Credit : Monica Schipper/Getty; CBS Photo Archive/Getty NEED TO KNOW Timothée Chalamet is the youngest actor since Marlon Brando to receive three Best Actor nominations at the OscarsChalamet, who turned 30 in December, was nominated for Best Actor for the third time on Jan. 22, for Marty SupremeBrando, who died in 2004 at 80, received three Oscar nominations by the time he was 30 and won his first Oscar on his fourth nomination for On the Waterfront Timothée Chalamet is joining rarified company after receiving his third Best Actor Oscar nomination. The star, who turned 30 in December, was nominated for Best Actor for Marty Supreme on Thursday, Jan. 22, when the 2026 Oscar nominations were announced. With that nomination, Chalamet is the youngest actor since Marlon Brando to receive three Best Actor nominations at the Academy Awards. Brando, who died at 80 in 2004, had received nominations in the movies A Streetcar Named Desire, Viva Zapata! and Julius Caesar by 1954, when he was 30. The actor won his first Oscar in 1955 for On the Waterfront and received four more nominations throughout his career, including another win for Best Actor for his performance in The Godfather in 1973. Chalamet also stands out as the only acting nominee in this year's field who was also nominated last year. In 2025, Chalamet was nominated for his portrayal of Bob Dylan in the biopic A Complete Unknown. (Adrien Brody ultimately won that award for his performance in The Brutalist.) Timothée Chalamet in Marty Supreme. Chalamet received his first Best Actor nomination at the Oscars in 2018 for his role in Call Me by Your Name. That year, Gary Oldman won for his portrayal of Winston Churchill in Darkest Hour. This year, Chalamet is nominated for Best Actor alongside Leonardo DiCaprio (One Battle After Another), Ethan Hawke (Blue Moon), Michael B. Jordan (Sinners) and Wagner Moura (The Secret Agent). Chalamet is also a double nominee this year: He is nominated as a producer for Marty Supreme as part of the movie's Best Picture nod alongside Josh Safdie, Ronald Bronstein, Eli Bush and Anthony Katagas. Marty Supreme received nine total nominations on Jan. 22. Sinners leads this year's pack with 16 total nominations, which broke a record for the most nominations for a single film ever, previously held by Titanic (1997), La La Land (2016) and All About Eve (1950) with 14 each. Timothée Chalamet in Marty Supreme. A24 Chalamet won awards for his Marty Supreme performance at the Critics Choice Awards and Golden Globe Awards earlier this month. He is also nominated at the 2026 Actor Awards (formerly the Screen Actors Guild Awards). In 2025, Chalamet won a SAG Award for his performance in A Complete Unknown, where he said in his speech that he wants "to be one of the greats" and name-checked Brando as an actor he is inspired by. Conan O'Brien is returning to host the Oscars live on Sunday, March 15, at 7 p.m. ET on ABC and streaming on Hulu.
